headline: High-risk workflow automation can overwrite shared files and propagate unverified outputs; prompt-injection risk is low because the course agent has no runtime channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable course repo with no io_surfaces, while agent B has files and workflow nodes but no documented direct ingestion channel from A. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or file handoff, so injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B workflow inputs without sanitization, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF B reads files produced from A as instructions, malicious content in those files can steer execution.
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template for B inputs.
Strip markdown/code fences before passing A output to B.
Review any copied text before execution.
Keep A outputs in read-only notes, not workflow fields.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read and write the server filesystem and call external APIs, while agent A has no runtime surfaces but may still supply content that B processes. Because B's default workflows can move whatever data they touch into integrations, shared-workspace leakage is plausible even though A itself is not a runtime agent.
conditions: IF B workflows process files that contain sensitive data from A-related materials, those contents can flow to external integrations.
IF the server filesystem is shared across workflows, B can read artifacts left by other jobs.
mitigations: Restrict B workflows to a dedicated directory.
Delete temporary files after each run.
Disable unnecessary integration nodes.
Store secrets only in the credential store.
Run a quick access review on the workflow filesystem paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, write_filesystem, and broad network egress, plus shared_state_with_other_instances via n8n datastore. Agent A has no runtime capabilities, so the conflict is one-sided but still dangerous: B can overwrite shared artifacts or race with other B instances in default orchestration.
conditions: IF two B instances target the same datastore key or filesystem path, writes can race.
IF Execute Command nodes touch shared files, one run can overwrite another run's artifacts.
mitigations: Assign unique run IDs to output paths.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Turn on per-workflow locking if available.
Separate credentials and datastores by environment.
Audit any Execute Command node for shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is an automation orchestrator that can act on workflow outputs, while agent A is a course repo whose content may be treated as authoritative by an operator or imported into B. If A-derived text is fed into B without verification, B can cascade errors into downstream actions or integrations.
conditions: IF A-derived instructions are used as workflow inputs, B may execute them as authoritative.
IF B nodes trigger external actions from those inputs, incorrect content can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before action nodes.
Require schema validation on all A-derived inputs.
Log provenance for every workflow field.
Block auto-execution on untrusted text.
Use a dry-run mode for new workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly handles whatever the workflow processes and stores secrets on the n8n server, while agent A is a public open-source course repo with no stated residency controls. The pair can therefore mix data classes under different retention or residency assumptions, but the evidence does not show a specific regulated class like PHI.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through B workflows, retention and residency obligations must be checked.
IF A-related materials are combined with customer data in B, policy mismatches can occur.
mitigations: Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows.
Document retention for each integration node.
Avoid storing sensitive data in workflow logs.
Review credential handling settings.
Add a data-class label to each workflow.
